about: Every difference between cua's output and the vendor's on these goldens, each with its cause (PROVENANCE.md). `fault` names where it comes from: "engine" (the recorded Skyshot is wrong, or lacks what the vendor reads), "redaction" (Finder's captures hide the content the rule reads) or "scene state" (the two lanes' actions left different states). The engine corrections (`kind: "skyshot"`, fault "engine") and the engine differences expire: M1b re-records these goldens live from the fixed engine (task M1a.2b) and deletes every engine-fault declaration then; one still needed at that point is an engine defect, not a declaration. Kinds: `skyshot` (a correction applied to the Skyshot before rendering), `part` (inside a matched line, cua's `<label>: <cua>` is the vendor's `<label>: <vendor>`), `missing` and `added` (a whole line, by its matching key), `header` and `trailer` (both sides' exact text), `addedOverTenPercent` (names its Decision Log entry). `golden` is "full", "before" or "diff" (all three when absent); `count` is exact.

declarations.cause: Engine (the flag's derivation; M1a.1's Walk.swift sets flags.disclosable whenever AXDisclosing is present). No vendor line in any capture prints `collapsed`: every web element of Chrome and Electron carries AXDisclosing false, and so do Finder's leaf rows, where the vendor prints neither flag nor an Expand action; the vendor prints `expanded` (and one 8-character secondary action, by its length SAICollapse's `Collapse`) on Finder's expanded sidebar sections. The vendor's own disclosable derivation is not read (sky-behaviour.md §23 item 2); the hypothesis the captures fit is AXDisclosing being settable. Applied to every scene: without it the renderer prints `(collapsed)` and `Secondary Actions: Expand` on 40 Chrome, 15 Electron and 40 Finder lines.

Engine (the flag's derivation; flags.settable is AXUIElementIsAttributeSettable(AXValue), which Chromium answers true for every native view and web control). The vendor prints `settable` on the text field, the text area and the tab (a Boolean value) and on none of the groups, toolbars, buttons, pop-up buttons, links, static texts, the tab group, the checkbox or the radio buttons; across all four scenes it prints it only on text fields and areas, a combo box, scroll bars, value indicators, ruler markers and Boolean values (the roles kept here). Its derivation is not read (sky-behaviour.md §23 item 2).
Engine, as Chrome's entry: Electron's native views (the window's nested groups) and the list box read settable; the vendor prints it on the text area only.

Engine (the Skyshot shape): valueType is "number" for every CFNumber, so a float whose value is integral renders `settable, integer` where the vendor prints `settable, float` from the CFNumber's type: TextEdit's two ruler markers at 0, Finder's scroll bars and value indicators at 0 and its splitter at 177 (each Finder line's length fits `float`, not `integer`). The roles are the ones the captures show; the fault is one, and the Skyshot should carry the CFNumber's type. The renderer takes "integer" or "float" when the engine names them.
Engine (the read set): the vendor prints the window's document as `URL: file:///…/cua-scene.rtf`; the engine's window node has no url (AXURL is read, AXDocument is not).

Engine (the read set), as TextEdit's entry: the vendor prints the window's `URL: 127.0.0.1:<port>/`. The URL set here is the cua run's page (the browser root view's url in the same Skyshot); the two lanes served the page on different ports.

Redaction, not rendering: the renderer drops an identifier that starts with `_` or `NS` [B §6], but the Finder captures replaced every identifier by its length, so the prefix is hidden and cua prints `ID: ⟨n⟩` where the vendor prints nothing. The 5-to-7-character identifiers (the two scroll areas, an outline and the two scroll bars; `_NS:<n>` by their length) are the ones whose vendor lines fit only without the part, each length needed; the longer identifiers print on both sides.
